extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to the Journal of Algebraic Combinatorics (Springer Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and manuscript-preparation rules and quality standards authors must follow when preparing and submitting research (and other) articles to the Journal of Algebraic Combinatorics. Covers title page, formatting, figures/tables, ethics, authorship, data, supplementary material, and post-acceptance steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be concise and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author information on title page
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide name(s) of author(s); affiliation(s) (institution, (department), city, (state), country); clear indication and active e-mail address of the corresponding author; if available, 16-digit ORCID of the author(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If address information is provided with affiliations it will be published. For temporarily unaffiliated authors only city and country are captured (not e-mail) unless requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an abstract of 150 to 250 words that does not contain undefined abbreviations or unspecified references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide 4 to 6 keywords for indexing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and Declarations inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Include required Statements and Declarations (e.g., Competing Interests) under the heading 'Statements and Declarations' in the published paper; submissions missing relevant declarations will be returned as incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See specific sections for examples of wording; revise/customize samples as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission implies the work has not been published before and is not under consideration elsewhere, and publication has been approved by all co-authors and responsible authorities at the institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher is not legally responsible for compensation claims arising from breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain permission from copyright owners for figures, tables, or text previously published elsewhere for both print and online formats and include evidence of such permission with submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material received without evidence will be assumed to originate from the authors. Some publishers may not grant electronic rights and costs to obtain permissions are not refundable by Springer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission and complete files
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload all manuscript files via the 'Submit manuscript' link and follow on-screen instructions; provide all relevant editable source files at every submission and revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to submit a complete set of editable source files will result in the article not being considered for review. For manuscript text submit common word processing formats such as .docx or LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Springer Nature LaTeX template / source requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For LaTeX submissions authors are encouraged to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template and submit the original source (including style files and figures) plus a PDF of the compiled output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word files are also accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Define abbreviations at first mention and use them consistently thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use footnotes to give additional information (may include citation of a reference included in the reference list); footnotes should not consist solely of a reference and must never include full bibliographic details; use footnotes (not endnotes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to text are numbered consecutively; footnotes to tables indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance values). Footnotes to title or authors are not given reference symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Place acknowledgments (people, grants, funds, etc.) in a separate section on the title page and write funding organization names in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference citation style in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference citations in the text should be identified by numbers in square brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for single citations, ranges, and multiple references (e.g., [1-3, 7]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list content and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference list should include only works cited in the text that have been published or accepted; entries should be numbered consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal communications and unpublished works should only be mentioned in text. Always include DOIs as full DOI links when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference formatting examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow provided examples for journal articles, articles by DOI, books, book chapters, and online documents (including use of standard journal abbreviations per ISSN LTWA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure, use full journal title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables numbering and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Number all tables using Arabic numerals and cite tables in text in consecutive numerical order; supply a table caption explaining the components of the table and identify previously published material with a reference at the end of the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to tables should be indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks) and included beneath the table body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic figure submission and file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all figures electronically and indicate which graphics program was used; preferred format for vector graphics is EPS; for halftones use TIFF; MSOffice files are also acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector graphics containing fonts must have embedded fonts. Name figure files with 'Fig' and the figure number (e.g., Fig1.eps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Line art technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For black-and-white line art use legible lines and lettering; all lines should be at least 0.1 mm (0.3 pt) wide; scanned line drawings/bitmap line drawings should have minimum resolution of 1200 dpi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone and combination artwork resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Halftone art (photographs, drawings with fine shading) should have minimum resolution of 300 dpi; combination art (halftone + line art, extensive lettering/color diagrams) should have minimum 600 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If magnification used in photographs indicate scale bars within the figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure lettering and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Helvetica or Arial (sans serif) for figure lettering; keep lettering consistently sized (about 2–3 mm, ~8–12 pt); minimal variance in type size within an illustration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid effects such as shading, outline letters; do not include titles or captions within illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Number all figures with Arabic numerals and cite them in text in consecutive numerical order; denote figure parts by lowercase letters (a, b, c, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appendix contains figures continue consecutive numbering of main text (do not use A1, A2); figures in online appendices (SI) should be numbered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure captions format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure should have a concise caption included in the text file (not in the figure file). Figure captions begin with the term 'Fig.' in bold followed by the figure number in bold, with no punctuation after the number and no terminal punctuation; identify all elements found in the figure and cite previously published material at the end of the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use boxes, circles, etc., as coordinate points in graphs and identify them in the caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure placement and size
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit figures within the body of the text; only submit large figures separately if file size prevents upload; size figures to fit column width with specified widths/heights for large- and small-sized journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widths/heights provided (e.g., 84 mm, 119 mm, 174 mm widths; height limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If including previously published figures, obtain permission for print and online and include evidence; if electronic rights unavailable, use other sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer will not refund permission costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure accessibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure figures are accessible: include descriptive captions; use patterns in addition to colors; any figure lettering must have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive captions help blind users with text-to-speech or Braille; check color->black-and-white legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI usage disclosure (text & images)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) do not satisfy authorship criteria; use of LLMs must be documented in the Methods (or suitable alternative) if used; Springer’s policy on generative AI images must be followed for images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-assisted copy editing for readability/style does not need to be declared (defined as improvements to human-generated text without autonomous content creation). There must be human accountability for final text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information (SI) submission formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer accepts electronic multimedia and other supplementary files (animations, movies, audio, etc.); supply SI in standard file formats and include article title, journal name, author names, affiliation and e-mail of corresponding author in each file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large files may cause long download times; collect multiple files in .zip or .gz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary multimedia technical specs
rubrics_metrics.description: For audio/video/animations use aspect ratio 16:9 or 4:3; maximum file size 2 GB; minimum video duration 1 second; supported formats: avi, wmv, mp4, mov, m2p, mp2, mpg, mpeg, flv, mxf, mts, m4v, 3gp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary text and spreadsheet formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit text and presentations in PDF (not .doc or .ppt for long-term viability); spreadsheets as .csv or .xlsx; specialized formats (.pdb, .wrl, .nb, .tex) may be supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A collection of figures can be combined in a PDF file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary numbering and citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention supplementary material in the manuscript as a citation (e.g., 'Online Resource 3'); name supplementary files consecutively (e.g., 'ESM_3.mpg', 'ESM_4.pdf') and provide concise captions for each file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SI will be published as received from the author without conversion, editing, or reformatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For accessibility ensure manuscript contains a descriptive caption for each supplementary material and video files do not contain flashes >3 times per second (to avoid seizure risk).

rubrics_metrics.name: MSC classification codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an appropriate number of Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) codes to categorize the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSC is used by Mathematical Reviews and Zentralblatt MATH; see www.ams.org/msc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of editing services is optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may use language/editing services (e.g., Springer Nature Author Services) for English editing, developmental comments, formatting, figure preparation, translation, etc., but such services are not required and do not guarantee acceptance or peer review selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A free Grammar Check tool is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific style for mathematical notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard mathematical notation: italic for single letters representing constants/variables/unknowns; roman/upright for numerals, operators, punctuation and commonly defined functions (e.g., cos, det, e, exp, lim, log, max, min, sin, tan, d for derivative); bold for vectors, tensors, and matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibility: originality, honesty, and good practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit to more than one journal simultaneously; work must be original and not previously published (unless an expansion); avoid salami-slicing; present results clearly and honestly without fabrication, falsification, or inappropriate data/image manipulation; adhere to discipline-specific rules for data acquisition/selection/processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal follows COPE guidelines on misconduct; examples of unacceptable practices and consequences provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibility: plagiarism and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not present others' data, text, or theories as your own; give proper acknowledgements, use quotation marks for verbatim copying, secure permissions for copyrighted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal may use software to screen for plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibility: citations and self-citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite appropriate and relevant literature to support claims; excessive or coordinated self-citation is strongly discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibility: avoid defamatory or untrue statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid untrue statements about entities or descriptions that could be seen as personal attacks or allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibility: dual-use and public safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify research that may be misapplied to pose threats to public health or national security (dual use) clearly in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include harmful biological agents, vaccine immune disruption, hazardous chemicals, weaponization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship correctness and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure author group, Corresponding Author, and author order are correct at submission and that all authors explicitly consent to submission before work is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding/deleting authors during revision is generally not permitted; changes must be explained and approved by Editor-in-Chief; no authorship changes after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship contribution criteria (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend authors meet the following: (1) substantial contributions to conception/design, data acquisition/analysis/interpretation, or creation of new software; (2) drafted or critically revised for intellectual content; (3) approved the version to be published; (4) agree to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on/adapted from ICMJE guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures and declarations (funding, ethics, consent, animal welfare)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include information on funding sources, financial/non-financial interests, ethics committee approvals for human/animal research, informed consent, and animal welfare statements as appropriate; include summary statements in a 'Declarations' section before references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding information must also be disclosed in the peer review system (added to Record of CrossMark but not the manuscript). Examples of wording for various cases are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and responsibilities of Corresponding Author
rubrics_metrics.description: One author is assigned as Corresponding Author who acts for all co-authors, ensures all listed authors have approved the manuscript and manages communication with the Journal before and after publication; they must ensure disclosures, declarations and data transparency statements are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managing communication may be delegated to a Contact/Submitting Author but Corresponding Author must be clearly indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contribution statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to include contribution statements specifying each author's contribution (free text or CRediT taxonomy) on a separate title page; for review articles state who had the idea, who did literature search/analysis, and who drafted or revised the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of free-text and CRediT-formatted statements are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation and author identification (ORCID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary affiliation should be the institution where the majority of work was done; current address may be additionally stated. Authors are recommended to use ORCID IDs when submitting or acquire one via submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names published exactly as on accepted submission; addresses will not be updated after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling deceased or incapacitated authors
rubrics_metrics.description: If a co-author dies or is incapacitated during writing/submission/review and co-authors wish to include them, obtain approval from a legal representative (e.g., direct relative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal will not investigate authorship disputes; authors should resolve disputes themselves; if unable, the Journal may withdraw a manuscript or raise the issue with authors' institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat all communication with the Journal (editors, handling editors, reviewers' reports) as confidential unless explicit consent to share has been received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to correct fundamental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must correct significant errors or inaccuracies discovered post-publication by contacting the journal and explaining the impact; correction or retraction decisions depend on the nature of the error and should provide transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction maintains the article on the platform watermarked as 'retracted' with an explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting and excluding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest suitable reviewers and/or request exclusion of certain individuals when submitting; suggested reviewers must be independent and not connected to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend a mix of reviewers from different countries/institutions; provide institutional email for suggested reviewers or other verification (homepage, publication record, researcher ID). The Journal may choose not to use suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure (authors, editors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must disclose financial or non-financial interests directly or indirectly related to the submitted work; disclose interests within the last 3 years of beginning the work (and older interests if they could reasonably be perceived as influencing the work). Editors and Editorial Board Members must declare competing interests and may be excluded from handling manuscripts where conflicts exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of funding, employment, financial, and non-financial interests are provided; a practical guideline is 'any undeclared financial interest that could embarrass the author if publicly known'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests: required statements and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary research and review articles require disclosure statements; other article types may require them depending on content. Provide explicit example phrasings for funded, unfunded, and interests-to-declare cases, or 'no competing interests' statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When all authors have the same/no conflicts a single blanket statement is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of requirements in 'Declarations' section
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize funding, competing interests, ethics approval, consent, data/material/code availability, and authors' contributions in a 'Declarations' section before the reference list under appropriate subheadings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See examples and customize wording as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance production and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: After acceptance the article goes to Production for typesetting; authors receive emails to confirm affiliation, choose publishing model, arrange rights and payments, and later a link to proofs. Proofs are for checking typesetting/conversion errors and completeness; substantial content changes are not allowed without editor approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After online publication further changes can only be made via an Erratum, which will be hyperlinked to the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article publishing agreement and copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on journal ownership/policy authors will either grant the Publisher an exclusive licence or transfer copyright; Open Choice OA articles do not require transfer of copyright and are published under a Creative Commons licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details of OA licences are on the journal's 'How to publish with us' guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour illustrations and offprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Online color illustrations are free; for print color authors may be expected to contribute to extra costs. Offprints can be ordered by the corresponding author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Choice (Open Access) option and APCs
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Choice allows open access publication in Springer Nature journals (APCs vary by journal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits listed (increased access, citations); links to funding/support pages provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Data Policy and Data Availability Statements (DAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal follows Springer Nature's research data policy; all original research must include a Data Availability Statement explaining how to access data supporting results, including links or citations to publicly archived datasets analysed or generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data cannot be shared publicly (e.g., privacy) the statement should describe access conditions; authors are encouraged to consider the minimal dataset necessary to interpret/replicate findings and to deposit supporting data in repositories where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data repositories and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to deposit supporting data in publicly available repositories (prefer discipline-specific repositories where available); the journal encourages open licences permitting reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For certain data types submission to specific public repositories is mandatory; ensure you have rights to share deposited data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite any publicly available data on which conclusions rely; data citations should include a persistent identifier (e.g., DOI) and follow DataCite minimum information (Dataset Creator, Title, Publisher [repository], Year, Identifier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data citations should be included in the reference list using the journal style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and peer review anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a journal uses double-anonymous peer review and authors provide reviewers with access to data, it is strongly suggested that authorship in the data is also anonymised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are repositories that can mask authorship or create masked links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and guidance for research data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who need help understanding data sharing policies, finding repositories, or organising and sharing research data can consult the Research Data Helpdesk and FAQ pages.
